content.title: About
content.content: Coffee substitute is a beverage made from roasted grains, roots, nuts or seeds that mimics the taste and aroma of traditional coffee but contains no caffeine. Common bases include barley, chicory, rye, cashews or sunflower seeds.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial coffee substitute appeared in Europe in the 19th century as “chicory coffee”.
Chicory is cultivated specifically for its root, which after roasting provides a characteristic bitter‑sweet flavor.
Barley coffee is popular in the Middle East and North Africa, where it is often served plain.
Coffee substitutes are widely used in vegan diets because they contain no animal products.
Some substitutes are fortified with B‑vitamins and minerals to compensate for the lack of caffeine.

items.title: Caffeine‑free
items.content: Suitable for people sensitive to caffeine or those who want to reduce their intake.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Roasted grains and roots provide fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Chicory and barley are rich in polyphenols, which help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports gut microbiota
items.content: Some substitutes contain prebiotic compounds that promote beneficial bacteria.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many coffee drinks with added cream, a plain substitute is virtually fat‑free.

items.title: Grain allergy
items.content: People allergic to wheat, barley or rye may react to grain‑based substitutes.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Certain substitutes (e.g., chicory) can contain oxalates, which may be problematic for those prone to kidney stones.

items.title: Added ingredients
items.content: Choose products without artificial flavors or added sugars to avoid extra calories and chemicals.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Prepare by pouring hot water (90‑95 °C) over 1‑2 tsp of the substitute per 200 ml of water, stir, and let steep for 2‑3 minutes. Add plant milk, spices (cinnamon, cardamom) or a sweetener to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct light. For long‑term storage, refrigerate to preserve aroma and prevent mold growth.
